analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Drugs is a commodity API manufacturer with razor-thin 6.16% operating margins, no durable pricing power, and profits that have nearly halved from their 2021 COVID-windfall peak of INR 280 Cr to INR 168 Cr in 2025. The valuation appears optically reasonable at 16.8x P/E, but the underlying business quality does not warrant ownership.
key_strengths: Manageable leverage at D/E 0.39 with no near-term solvency risk
Promoter skin-in-the-game at 55% holding signals alignment
Diversified API portfolio (NSAIDs, fluoroquinolones, antidiabetics) reduces single-product concentration risk
key_risks: Revenue contraction two consecutive years (2024: INR 2,529 Cr → 2025: INR 2,387 Cr) after peaking at INR 2,716 Cr — the trend is going the wrong way
Operating margins at 6.16% confirm commodity pricing with no moat — APIs face relentless Chinese competition and customer bargaining power
FCF is erratic and thin: INR 67 Cr in 2025 despite INR 177 Cr capex, while borrowings remain elevated at INR 573 Cr with minimal cash (INR 5 Cr)
red_flags: Net profit collapsed 40% from 2021 peak (INR 280 Cr) to INR 168 Cr — the COVID API supercycle masked structural weakness
ROE of 12.7% is below my 15% minimum threshold, and contracting EBITDA (INR 490 Cr in 2021 → INR 307 Cr in 2025) shows the business is not earning adequate returns on expanding assets
Large CWIP (INR 179-261 Cr range over 3 years) hasn't translated into earnings improvement — capital is being consumed without commensurate return
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aarti Drugs epitomizes what I call a "fair business at a fair price" — and I have no interest in either. The company's 9-year revenue CAGR of 8.6% looks passable, but the 2021 peak (INR 2,155 Cr → INR 440 Cr operating income) was entirely a COVID-era API shortage windfall, not a reflection of sustainable competitive advantage. Since that peak, operating income has contracted from INR 440 Cr to INR 290 Cr while revenues have also shrunk — the business is running faster just to fall further behind. A 6.16% operating margin is a confession that this is a commodity business where no one can sustainably price above cost of production.

The capital allocation story troubles me further. The company has spent INR 720 Cr in capex over 2022-2025 while generating cumulative FCF of roughly INR 87 Cr over the same period — capital is being destroyed, not created. Debt has risen from INR 351 Cr (2021) to INR 615 Cr (2025) to fund this expansion, yet ROCE sits at 13.1% and ROE at 12.7%. I want to own businesses that generate cash, not consume it. At 16.8x P/E, the market is not demanding an unreasonable price — but I require a wonderful business, not merely a reasonably priced mediocre one. This stays firmly outside my circle of interest.
